selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What three strong qualities did the passage say he showed while calling people to the truth?
questions.answer: He showed strong patience, firmness, and bravery.

questions.question: How serious was the opposition against him?
questions.answer: It was very serious and harsh, coming from many sides.

questions.question: Why is his courage especially impressive in this passage?
questions.answer: Because the opposition came from large powers and also from people close to him.

questions.question: How does the passage describe his faith in relation to the whole world?
questions.answer: It says his faith spread light to the whole world.

questions.question: How many tiny doubts were others able to place in his faith?
questions.answer: They were not able to place even the smallest doubt in it.

questions.question: What failed to shake his confidence?
questions.answer: The dominant beliefs of the time, philosophical ideas, and religious teachings failed to shake it.

questions.question: What feelings were unable to enter his faith?
questions.answer: Doubt, hesitation, weakness, and anxiety could not enter it.

questions.question: What final judgment did the traveler make with his mind?
questions.answer: He became sure that falsehood and trickery could not belong to such a person.

questions.question: Which part of his life is not used alone, but joined with others to prove truthfulness?
questions.answer: His worship is joined with his law, prayer, call, and faith to prove truthfulness.

questions.question: In this passage, what part of his mission is discussed first?
questions.answer: First, it talks about how he delivered the message and called people to the truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about his level of fear during this struggle?
questions.answer: It says he showed no sign of fear.

questions.question: What happened in the end that points to the power of his message?
questions.answer: Islam rose to a place of great strength in the world.

questions.question: What larger proof is given from the outcome of his mission?
questions.answer: The larger proof is that he overcame opposition and Islam became victorious in the world.

questions.question: How is his faith different from normal human confidence?
questions.answer: It is described as extraordinary, deeply certain, and amazingly wide.

questions.question: What kinds of ideas could not shake his belief?
questions.answer: The beliefs, philosophies, and teachings that were common in the world at that time could not weaken his faith.

questions.question: Name two areas listed at the end that support his truthfulness.
questions.answer: Two of them are his worship and his call to the truth.

questions.question: How did saintly people after them view him?
questions.answer: They viewed him as the highest example of faith and drew from his belief.

questions.question: Why does the traveler decide that lying and cheating do not fit such a person?
questions.answer: Because someone with such a unique religion, worship, prayer, call to truth, and faith would not be a liar or deceiver.

questions.question: What did he keep doing even when many enemies opposed him?
questions.answer: He kept delivering the message and inviting people to the truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the kind of enemies he faced?
questions.answer: He faced both outside enemies and people from his own community and family.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention his own tribe and uncle?
questions.answer: It mentions them to show that even close relationships did not stop him from the truth.

questions.question: What world-level change is mentioned as evidence of his successful mission?
questions.answer: The passage says Islam became the leading power in the world.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the strength of his faith?
questions.answer: It says his faith was amazingly strong, wide, and full of certainty.

questions.question: How did the Companions and later saintly people connect to his faith?
questions.answer: They took from his example and saw him as the highest model of belief.
